response: Yes, infundibular height can be a useful predictor for the clearance of lower pole calyceal stones after extracorporeal shockwave lithotripsy (ESWL). According to the available data, a lower infundibular height, specifically less than 22 mm, suggests a good outcome from lithotripsy, indicating that patients with this measurement may benefit from ESWL treatment. This measurement can serve as a tool to decide which patients are likely to have a successful outcome from the procedure.
